what: Sort Lines puts any list in order. Paste one item per line and pick an order: alphabetical, reverse alphabetical, natural (item2 before item10), by the numbers in each line, by length, reversed, or shuffled at random.

It helps anyone who works with lists: names for a class or team, keywords, product codes, file names, references, to-do items or rows copied from a spreadsheet. It can also remove duplicates, empty lines and stray spaces in the same step.
Sorting respects the alphabet of your language and runs in your browser, so your list is never uploaded.
uses: Put a class list, guest list or team roster in A to Z order.
Sort scores, prices or measurements from smallest to largest, even when each line has words around the number.
Use natural order so chapter2 comes before chapter10.
Shuffle names for presentations, raffles or turns in a game.
Remove duplicates and empty lines while sorting.
tutorial: Put each item on its own line in the top box. A column copied from a spreadsheet works directly.

A to Z and Z to A sort alphabetically. Natural treats numbers inside text by value. Numbers sorts by the first number in each line. Length sorts by the number of characters. Character code sorts strictly by computer code, which developers sometimes need.
Reverse flips the current order, Shuffle mixes the lines randomly, and Keep the current order only applies the clean-up options.
Ignore upper/lower case makes Apple and apple equal. Remove duplicates keeps only the first copy of each line. Remove empty lines and Trim spaces tidy the list.
The result updates as you type. A message shows how many lines went in and out and how many duplicates were removed.
Click Copy result, Download .txt, or Use result as input to sort it again another way.
features: Alphabetical, natural, numeric, length, character code, reverse, shuffle and more.
Accented letters and non-Latin alphabets sort the way people expect.
Understands negatives, decimals and thousands separators such as 1,234.5 or 12,5.
Uses secure randomness, with a Shuffle again button.
Remove duplicates, empty lines and extra spaces in one go.
Handles hundreds of thousands of lines.

example.title: Worked example: sorting scores
example.text: Paste: Maya 87, Leo 9, Sam 100, Ana 45 (each on its own line). With A to Z you get Ana 45, Leo 9, Maya 87, Sam 100. Switch the order to Numbers, largest first and the list becomes Sam 100, Maya 87, Ana 45, Leo 9. Click Copy result to paste it into your report.

tips: Use Natural instead of A to Z for numbered items like Chapter 1 to Chapter 20.
Untick Ignore upper/lower case if Apple and apple must stay separate when removing duplicates.
Choose Keep the current order to only remove duplicates and empty lines without sorting.
Use result as input lets you combine sorts, for example shuffle first and then sort by length.
For a spreadsheet with several columns, sort inside the spreadsheet instead, so rows stay together.
problems: Numbers are in the wrong order with A to Z
Alphabetical order compares character by character, so 10 comes before 9. Choose Natural or Numbers.
Some lines went to the end with Numbers
Those lines contain no number. They are kept at the end in their original order.
Tick Remove duplicates. If the lines differ only by spaces, keep Trim spaces on; if only by capital letters, tick Ignore upper/lower case.
It does not update while I type
Lists longer than about 300,000 characters are sorted only when you click Sort lines, to keep typing smooth.
